questions.q: Instrument fitted in the carburetor of the automobile to provide the correct mixture of air and fuel necessary for combustion works on
questions.explanation: The venturi-like narrowing in a carburetor speeds up the air, lowering its pressure by Bernoulli's principle, which draws in fuel to mix with the air. KEA's revised key (dated 10-05-2026) awarded grace marks to all candidates for this question; Bernoulli's Principle remains the physically correct answer.

questions.q: In a capillary tube experiment, a vertical 30 cm long capillary tube is dipped in water, water rises upto a height of 10 cm due to capillarity. If this experiment is conducted in a freely falling elevator, then the length of the water column becomes
questions.explanation: In free fall, effective gravity is zero, and since capillary rise height ∝ 1/g$_{eff}$, water rises to fill the entire length of the tube, i.e., 30 cm.

questions.q: A horizontal pipe carries water in a streamlined flow. At a point along the pipe, where the cross-sectional area is 10 cm$^2$, the velocity of water is 1 ms$^{-1}$ and the pressure is 2000 Pa. What is the pressure of water at another point where the cross-sectional area is 5 cm$^2$? [Density of water = 1000 kgm$^{-3}$]
questions.explanation: By continuity, $v_2=10(1)/5=2\,ms^{-1}$. By Bernoulli's equation, $P_2=P_1+\tfrac12\rho(v_1^2-v_2^2)=2000+500(1-4)=500$ Pa.

questions.q: While determining the coefficient of viscosity of the given liquid, a spherical steel ball sinks by a distance h = 0.9 m. The radius of the ball is r = $\sqrt3\times10^{-3}$m. The time taken by the ball to sink in three trials are tabulated as follows. Trial 1: 2.75 s, Trial 2: 2.65 s, Trial 3: 2.70 s. The difference between the densities of the steel ball and the liquid is 7000 kg m$^{-3}$. If g = 10.0 ms$^{-2}$, then the coefficient of viscosity of the given liquid at room temperature is
questions.explanation: Average time $=2.70$ s, so $v=h/t=0.9/2.7=1/3\,ms^{-1}$. By Stokes' law, $\eta=\dfrac{2r^2\Delta\rho\,g}{9v}=\dfrac{2(3\times10^{-6})(7000)(10)}{9(1/3)}\approx0.14$ Pa.s.

questions.q: Water flows through a horizontal pipe of varying cross-section at a rate of $0.314\,m^3s^{-1}$. The velocity of water at a point where the radius of the pipe is 10 cm is
questions.explanation: $Q=Av\Rightarrow0.314=\pi(0.1)^2\times v\Rightarrow v=10\,ms^{-1}$.

questions.q: A closed water tank has cross-sectional area A. It has a small hole at a depth of h from the free surface of water [tank of pressure P$_0$ above the water, height H to the hole, hole of radius r at depth h from the surface]. The radius of the hole is r so that $r \ll \sqrt{A/\pi}$. If P$_0$ is the pressure inside the tank above water level, and P$_a$ is the atmospheric pressure, the rate of flow of the water coming out of the hole is [ρ is the density of water]
questions.explanation: By Bernoulli's theorem, the efflux speed is $v=\sqrt{2gh+2(P_0-P_a)/\rho}$, so the volume flow rate is $\pi r^2 v$.

questions.q: Two capillary tubes P and Q are dipped vertically in water. The height of water level in capillary tube P is $\dfrac{2}{3}$ of the height in capillary tube Q. The ratio of their diameter is ______.
questions.explanation: Since $h\propto \dfrac{1}{d}$, $\dfrac{h_P}{h_Q}=\dfrac{d_Q}{d_P}=\dfrac23 \Rightarrow \dfrac{d_P}{d_Q}=\dfrac32$, i.e. 3:2.

questions.q: Iceberg floats in water with part of it submerged. What is the fraction of the volume of iceberg submerged if the density of ice is $\rho_i=0.917$ g cm$^{-3}$?
questions.explanation: By flotation, the submerged fraction equals $\rho_{ice}/\rho_{water}=0.917/1=0.917$.

questions.q: [Figure shows a cylindrical container filled with water, with a small hole on the side at height H = 8 cm from the bottom and at depth h = 2 cm below the top water surface] A cylindrical container containing water has a small hole at height of H = 8 cm from the bottom and at a depth of 2 cm from the top surface of the liquid. The maximum horizontal distance travelled by the water before it hits the ground (x) is
questions.explanation: Efflux speed $v=\sqrt{2gh}$ with h = 2 cm, and time to fall height H = 8 cm is $t=\sqrt{2H/g}$; range $x = vt = 2\sqrt{hH} = 2\sqrt{2\times8} = 8$ cm.

questions.q: An aluminium sphere is dipped into water. Which of the following is true ?
options: Buoyancy will be less in water at 0 $^\circ$C than that in water at 4 $^\circ$C
Buoyancy will be more in water at 0 $^\circ$C than that in water at 4 $^\circ$C
Buoyancy in water at 0 $^\circ$C will be same as that in water at 4 $^\circ$C
Buoyancy may be more or less in water at 4 $^\circ$C depending on the radius of the sphere
questions.explanation: Water has its maximum density at 4 $^\circ$C, so the buoyant force (which depends on fluid density) is greater there than at 0 $^\circ$C, making buoyancy at 0 $^\circ$C less than at 4 $^\circ$C.

questions.q: The pressure at the bottom of a liquid tank is not proportional to the
questions.explanation: Pressure at the bottom, P = h$\rho$g, depends on height, density and g, but is independent of the surface area of the liquid.

questions.q: 'Hydraulic lift' works on the basis of
questions.explanation: A hydraulic lift uses Pascal's law: pressure applied at one point of an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally to all points, allowing a small force to lift a large load.

questions.q: An ideal fluid flows through a pipe of circular cross section with diameters 5 cm and 10 cm as shown. The ratio of velocities of fluid at A and B is [Figure: fluid enters a cone-shaped pipe at the narrow end A (diameter 5 cm) and leaves at the wide end B (diameter 10 cm)]
questions.explanation: By continuity, $v \propto 1/d^2$. $v_A/v_B = (d_B/d_A)^2 = (10/5)^2 = 4:1$.

questions.q: A flow of liquid is streamline if the Reynold number is
questions.explanation: Flow is streamline (laminar) for Reynolds number less than about 1000.

questions.q: Two solids P and Q float in water. It is observed that P floats with half of its volume immersed and Q floats with $\dfrac{2}{3}^{rd}$ of its volume is immersed. The ratio of densities of P and Q is
questions.explanation: For a floating body, the fraction immersed equals the ratio of its density to water's density: $\rho_P=0.5\rho_w$, $\rho_Q=\dfrac23\rho_w$, so $\rho_P:\rho_Q=0.5:\dfrac23=3:4$.

questions.q: Spheres of iron and lead having same mass are completely immersed in water. Density of lead is more than that of iron. Apparent loss of weight is W$_1$ for iron sphere and W$_2$ for lead sphere. Then $\dfrac{W_1}{W_2}$ is
questions.explanation: Loss of weight equals the weight of water displaced, $\rho_wVg$; for equal mass, $V=m/\rho$, so the less dense iron sphere has a larger volume and hence a larger loss of weight, giving W$_1$/W$_2$ > 1.

questions.q: Eight equal drops of water are falling through air with a steady velocity of 10 cm $s^{-1}$. If the drops combine to form a single drop big in size, then the terminal velocity of this big drop is .................
questions.explanation: Volume conservation gives $R=2r$ for 8 drops combining; terminal velocity $\propto r^2$, so $v_{big}=10\times2^2=40$ cm $s^{-1}$.

questions.q: Two capillary tubes of different diameters are dipped in water. The rise of water is .........
options: greater in the tube of larger diameter
greater in the tube of smaller diameter
independent of the diameter of the tube
questions.explanation: Capillary rise $h = \dfrac{2T\cos\theta}{r\rho g}$ is inversely proportional to the tube radius, so the rise is greater in the tube of smaller diameter.

questions.q: Three liquids of equal masses are taken in three identical cubical vessels $A$, $B$ and $C$. Their densities are $P_A$, $P_B$ and $P_C$ respectively. But $P_A < P_B < P_C$. The force exerted by the liquid on the base of the cubical vessel is .......................
options: the same in all the vessels
questions.explanation: The force on the base equals the weight of the liquid, $mg$, which is the same for all three vessels since the masses are equal, regardless of density.

questions.q: Water is in streamline flow along a horizontal pipe with nonuniform cross-section. At a point in the pipe where the area of cross-section is 10 cm$^2$, the velocity of water is 1 ms$^{-1}$ and the pressure is 2000 Pa. The pressure at another point where the cross-sectional area is 5 cm$^2$ is .....................
questions.explanation: By continuity, $v_2=A_1v_1/A_2=10\times1/5=2$ ms$^{-1}$. By Bernoulli's theorem, $P_2=P_1+\tfrac12\rho(v_1^2-v_2^2)=2000+500(1-4)=500$ Pa.

questions.q: Horizontal tube of non-uniform cross-section has radii of 0.1 m and 0.05 m respectively at M and N [a converging tube with a wide bore at M and narrow bore at N]. For a streamline flow of liquid the rate of liquid flow is
options: greater at M than at N
greater at N than at M
questions.explanation: By the equation of continuity, the volume flow rate $Av$ is constant along a streamline tube, so it is the same at M and N.

questions.q: Two solid pieces, one of steel and the other of aluminium when immersed completely in water have equal weights. When the solid pieces are weighed in air
options: the weight of aluminium is half the weight of steel
questions.explanation: Equal apparent weight in water means $W_1\left(1-\dfrac{\rho_w}{\rho_1}\right)=W_2\left(1-\dfrac{\rho_w}{\rho_2}\right)$. Since steel's density $\rho_1$ is much greater than aluminium's $\rho_2$, the factor $\left(1-\rho_w/\rho_1\right)$ is larger for steel, so its true weight $W_1$ must be smaller to match; hence the aluminium piece weighs more in air.
